finding: The live range of $1,075-$3,700 starts too low and tops out a little low for trucks. Built totals (parts + stated hours x $120-$160/hr, the national middle labor rate used for these checks): economy 2015 Corolla about $1,617-$3,301 (11.5-18.8 hr); midsize 2016 Camry about $1,704-$3,044 (11.5-17.0 hr); truck 2012 F-150 5.0L, both heads, about $2,842-$4,349 (20.9-24.2 hr); luxury 2015 BMW 328i could not be totalled because no stated labor time was found (parts alone $274-$407). The lowest total we can build is about $1,600, and that already uses a manufacturer warranty time and online parts prices with no machine-shop work, coolant or oil, so real quotes start higher; nothing supports $1,075. At the top, both heads on a full-size truck come to about $4,350, above $3,700. A range of roughly $1,600-$4,400 fits the evidence better. RepairPal ($2,572-$3,386 national; F-150 $3,474-$4,603) and CarParts.com ($2,400-$3,200) sit inside our built totals; only a 2023 J.D. Power article ($1,000-$3,000) supports the live low end. How solid the labor times are: none is a manufacturer time for the example vehicle. The economy and midsize low ends are Honda warranty flat-rate times for comparable cars (11.5 hr for the 2016-17 Civic 1.5L turbo and for the 2018-22 Accord 1.5L turbo; other Honda bulletins give 10.8-12.4 hr), not Toyota times. The economy high end (18.8 hr) is a technician forum post quoting a labor guide for the sister 1.8L engine in a Prius, and the midsize high end (17 hr) is a parts retailer's statement about Camrys with no model years given; both are weak. The truck times are Ford warranty times for replacing both cylinder heads on an F-150 with the 2.7L V6 (20.9-24.2 hr), not the 5.0L V8; a technician forum post puts the 5.0L book time at about 24 hours, which agrees. Other caveats: the midsize parts figure is a single aftermarket set price without head bolts; the truck bolt-set listing does not say whether it covers both heads; fluids were not priced.
extras: Machine-shop work is the biggest add-on: the head is normally checked for flatness and cracks and resurfaced, and a warped or cracked head means more machining or a replacement head. Quotes also commonly add coolant, engine oil and filter, thermostat, spark plugs, a diagnosis fee (cooling-system pressure test or combustion-gas test), shop supplies and sales tax. Many shops recommend doing the timing chain or belt, water pump and related seals while the engine is apart, and V engines may be quoted for one head or both, so check which the quote covers.
